title: Burst credit hedging and metering: rules, reconciliation, and invoice clarity
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem: Customers who oscillate between steady reserved usage and short unpredictable spikes (e.g., marketing campaigns, month-end jobs) are confused by current burst behavior: credits are consumed unevenly across routes, invoices show opaque lineitems, and automation that reallocates burst capacity causes surprise overage charges. This PRD defines rules for 'burst credit hedging' to: 1) provide predictable short-term burst capacity for customers with mixed reserved and hosted usage; 2) meter and report consumption consistently across routes and models; and 3) produce predictable invoice line items and reconciliation flows so finance and customers can audit charges.
scope: Design hedging rules for short burst windows (1m/15m/24h), define metering semantics for pooled burst credits vs per-route credits, implement transparent invoice grouping and reason codes, and add reconciliation acceptance tests. Includes API knobs (burst window, hedging threshold) surfaced in Console and billing UI. Implementation spans billing metering pipeline and billing UI; requires ENG changes to quota allocator and metering export format.
out_of_scope: Full subscription re-pricing, enterprise reserved-contract renegotiation, deep discounts for long-term commitments, and changes to core rate-per-token pricing. Complex cross-account credit swaps (multi-tenant pooling) will be handled in a follow-up.
requirements: Define hedging policy: allow plan-level config for 'hedge_ratio' (0-100%) that reserves a percentage of transient burst capacity for customers with fluctuating usage
Burst windows supported: 60s, 15m, 24h. Each window has separate counters and retention semantics
Metering: every token/embedding request must be annotated with 'burst_pool_id' and 'hedge_flag' at export time for reconciliation
Invoice grouping: line items must show (a) reserved usage, (b) hedged burst consumed, (c) unhedged burst/overage with reason codes
Roll-forward behavior: unused hedged credits expire at window end and are not refundable; but invoice footnote must show expired hedged credits for transparency
Fail-safe: when hedged pool exhausted, requests fall back to standard quota/overage with explicit reason code; system must not silently drop requests
Admin UI: show hedged pool utilization by window in Console (per-customer) and provide export of raw counters for finance
Audit logs: every automatic reallocation or hedging credit draw must produce an auditable event with timestamps and request IDs
Backwards compatibility: existing customers default hedge_ratio=0 (no change in behavior)
acceptance_criteria: Billing export format updated and validated: hedged_usage and hedged_expiry columns present and match internal counters for 60s/15m/24h windows
End-to-end test: synthetic workload with known spike pattern produces expected hedged consumption and invoice grouping in staging (counts within 0.5% of expected tokens)
Console shows hedged-pool charts with correct utilization and hover text explaining reason codes
API: new billing metering annotation fields accepted by hosted endpoints and present in Kafka export (schema v3). Schema validated with contract tests
Finance reconciliation: sample invoice for a test tenant includes separate line items for hedged credits, expired hedged credits, and overage; finance team sign-off documented in comments
Failover path verified: when hedged pool depletes mid-spike, requests continue to be served and overage line items are created with 'HEDGE_EXHAUSTED' reason code
Security: audit events for hedged draws are logged to existing secure audit stream; no PII is added
Performance: metering overhead adds <2% p99 latency to token path in staging; ENG sign-off required
success_metrics: Reduce customer billing disputes related to burst usage by >=60% in first 90 days after rollout
At least 75% of existing bursty customers opt in to non-zero hedge_ratio within 60 days after release
Metering accuracy within 0.5% between runtime counters and billing export over 24h test
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Implement metering schema changes and Console surface; run contract tests and synthetic spike scenarios. Phase 2 (canary): Enable hedge_ratio=10% for 5 pilot customers (self-serve opt-in) and monitor billing export + customer feedback for 2 weeks. Phase 3 (general availability): default hedge_ratio=0 but provide in-product toggle; announce with billing FAQ and support playbook. Finance will run a reconciliation job for first 2 billing cycles to flag anomalies.
